Treatment summary
The patient presented following a rear-end motor veihcle collision with neck pain, stiffness, and headache consistent
with cervical whiplash injury. The mechanism of injury described is entirely plausible for the force involved in this type
of crash. Over the course of 27 visits, care included examination, targeted physical therapy, and home exercise
instruction. Imaging and physical examination findings clearly confirm soft tissue injury to the cervical spine, with
reduced ragne of motion and paraspinal tenderness documented at initial evaluation. Treatment followed a usual and
expected course, with visit frequency tapering as symptoms steadily improved and range of motion returned toward
baseline. No prior injury or treatment to the same body region is known to this provider. Billed services correspond to
the care documented in the clinical notes, with no repeated or duplicate charges identified. Prognosis is good with
continued home exercise.
